note: Questions from the CBSE Class X English (Language and Literature) board exam 2025, Q.P. code 2/1/1, published by CBSE at cbse.gov.in. Q7(a) is left out because its last part has no correct option. The writing task in Q5(a) is given as text (the original shows a chart). Model answers are written for this portal and are not CBSE's official marking scheme.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Read the following passage carefully :
(1) Saffron is a spice that's long been revered across the globe, captivating hearts and palates with its deep-red hue and complex flavour. It is one of the most prized spices that you can find on this planet. Just like gold is among the most valuable metals in the world, saffron means the same in the world of spices. Also known as 'kesar' in Hindi, it has a rich history and is often called an ancient spice. Saffron is being used since ages in various foods made for the royals and the elite as it contains medicinal properties.
(2) Originating from the delicate stigma of the saffron crocus flower, it transforms the ordinary into the extraordinary, infusing dishes with a subtle, earthy sweetness that adds a special taste to the palate. Saffron has a strong exotic aroma and a unique flavour and is used to colour and flavour many Mediterranean and Asian dishes, particularly rice, fish and English, Scandinavian, and Balkan breads.
(3) Saffron forms the backbone of several iconic dishes from around the world, such as the Spanish rice, seafood dish Paella, the French stew Bouillabaisse, Italian rice dish Risotto Milanese, the Indian ice cream Kesar Kulfi, Pakistani rice dish Biryani, and baked Iranian rice Tachin. Saffron's rich red colour is attributed to crocin; its bitter taste, to picrocrocin; and its distinctive aroma, to safranal.
(4) Saffron is cultivated chiefly in Iran but is also grown in Spain, France, Italy, and parts of India. A labour-intensive crop, the three stigmas are handpicked from each flower, spread on trays, and dried over charcoal fires for use as a food flavouring and colouring agent.
(5) Most historians speculate it was first domesticated in Iran, but south-western Greek islands remain strong contenders. Traders, conquerors, and world explorers introduced it to China, India and the Middle East. From there, it travelled to Mediterranean Europe.
(6) The high retail value of saffron is maintained in world markets because of labour-intensive harvesting methods, which require some 444,000 hand-picked saffron stigmas per kilogram — equivalently, 150,000 crocus flowers per kilogram. Forty hours of labour are needed to pick 150,000 flowers. Almost all saffron grows in a belt from Spain in the west to India in the east. Iran is responsible for around 88% of global production. Afghanistan comes second, and Spain is the third largest producer, while the United Arab Emirates, Greece, the Indian subcontinent and Morocco are among minor producers.
(7) Given its high price, adulteration is quite common, unfortunately. Adulterants like beetroot or pomegranate are used to enhance red colour; silk fibres, oil, or wax are used to add bulk, and powdered saffron can be adulterated with turmeric and paprika.

Answer the following questions :
(i) What is the tone of the writer in the line "Saffron is being used since ages in various foods made for the royals and the elite as it contains medicinal properties." ? Rationalise your response in about 40 words. (1)
(ii) Which statement best describes the comparison "Just like gold is among the most valuable metals in the world, saffron means the same in the world of spices." ? (A) Gold and saffron have similar physical properties. (B) Gold and saffron have equal monetary value. (C) Saffron is considered the most valuable spice, similar to how gold is valued among metals. (D) Gold and saffron are both rare commodities in the global market. (1)
(iii) List any two points why saffron is revered across the globe. (Paragraphs 2 and 3) (2)
(iv) In the phrase 'backbone of several iconic dishes', the word 'iconic' refers to : (A) delicately cooked (B) widely recognized (C) peculiar and rare (D) strange and infamous (1)
(v) Complete the sentence : Saffron has a labour-intensive cultivation process which involves ______. (2)
(vi) True or False : According to historians, saffron was first used in the kitchens in Iran. (1)
(vii) Which statement best describes the reason for saffron's high retail value ? (A) Due to its magical or mystical properties. (B) Because it can only be grown in specific regions. (C) Due to its labour-intensive cultivation process and its relatively low yield per plant. (D) Because traders, conquerors, and world explorers hoard it. (1)
(viii) Support the writer's view with evidence from the text that saffron is often adulterated. (1)
questions.solution: (i) Appreciative/admiring: the writer praises saffron as a prized spice fit for royals and the elite and valued for its medicinal properties. (ii) (C). (iii) Any two: its deep-red colour and strong, exotic aroma; its unique flavour that turns ordinary food into something special; it is the backbone of iconic dishes around the world. (iv) (B) widely recognized. (v) hand-picking the three stigmas from each flower, spreading them on trays and drying them over charcoal fires. (vi) False: historians only speculate that it was first domesticated (grown) in Iran. (vii) (C). (viii) Beetroot or pomegranate are added for colour, silk fibres, oil or wax for bulk, and powdered saffron is mixed with turmeric and paprika.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Read the following passage carefully :
(1) Silk is a natural protein fibre, some forms of which can be woven into textiles. Silk has a long history in India. It is known as Resham in eastern and northern India, and Pattu in the southern parts of India. India is the second largest producer of silk in the world after China.
(2) Silk is renowned for its luxurious qualities with a natural soft and smooth texture that feels comfortable on the skin. One of its unique qualities is to absorb and release moisture, regulating the body temperature, and keeping the wearer cool and dry.
(3) Silk is one of the strongest natural fibres, but it loses up to 20% of its strength when wet. Its elasticity is moderate to poor: if elongated even a small amount, it remains stretched. It can be weakened if exposed to too much sunlight. It may also be attacked by insects, especially if left dirty.
(4) The process of silk production is known as sericulture. Silk is produced by several insects; but, generally, only the silk of moth caterpillars has been used for textile manufacturing. To produce 1 kg of silk, 104 kg of mulberry leaves must be eaten by 3000 silkworms.
(5) So what makes silk so costly ? Firstly, cultivation of silk is a labour-intensive work. Secondly, the silk fabric is carefully derived from the larva of the silkworms which spin silk threads around themselves to make cocoons from natural sources. This makes the production limited due to factors like climate, availability of quality mulberry leaves and time required by silkworms to complete their lifecycle. Thirdly, the intensive work can only be carried out with specialized knowledge and expertise by skilled artisans and craftsmanship. Lastly, superior quality silk fabrics are made from long and uniform silk fibres giving them a smooth and lustrous appearance. Thus, production requires careful selection, adding to the cost.
In 2021, Karnataka was the highest producer of raw silk at 8483 metric tonnes followed by Andhra Pradesh at 5520 metric tonnes with Assam close behind at 5038 metric tonnes. At the other end of the spectrum there was Chhattisgarh (248 metric tonnes), Nagaland (230 metric tonnes) and UP trailed behind at 179 metric tonnes.

Answer the following questions :
(i) What does the phrase 'luxurious qualities' in paragraph (2) tell you about the silk fabric ? Write in 40 words with evidence from the text. (2)
(ii) Assertion : Silk production requires careful selection. Reason : Long and uniform silk fibres give silk a glossy appearance. (A) Both true, reason explains assertion. (B) Both true, reason does not explain assertion. (C) Assertion true, reason false. (D) Assertion false, reason true. (1)
(iii) Justify : Silk whispers luxury! Its price reflects not just its rarity but the value of the meticulous process behind its creation. (1)
(iv) Mention the top two countries that produce silk. (1)
(v) "Factors like climate, availability of quality mulberry leaves and time required by silkworms to complete their lifecycle are important factors for the production of silk." State any one inference that can be drawn from this. (1)
(vi) Complete with a suitable reason from the text : Though silk is considered one of the strongest fibres, it is ______. (1)
(vii) Mention the states which produced the most and the least amount of raw silk in India in 2021. (1)
(viii) Complete : 104 kgs of mulberry leaves eaten by 3000 silkworms results in ______. (1)
(ix) Give one reason why silk production is considered labour-intensive. (1)
questions.solution: (i) It suggests silk is rich and comfortable: it has a natural soft, smooth texture that feels comfortable on the skin, and it absorbs and releases moisture, regulating body temperature and keeping the wearer cool and dry. (ii) (A). (iii) Silk is costly because making it takes careful, skilled, labour-intensive work: silkworms must be reared on quality mulberry leaves, cocoons handled carefully and the best fibres selected. (iv) China and India. (v) Silk production depends on natural conditions, so its supply is limited (and it cannot be produced quickly or everywhere). (vi) weakened when wet (it loses up to 20% of its strength), or by too much sunlight. (vii) Most: Karnataka; least: Uttar Pradesh. (viii) 1 kg of silk. (ix) Any one: silk has to be carefully taken from the cocoons the silkworms spin; it needs skilled artisans with special knowledge; the fibres must be carefully selected.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Fill in the blank using the correct form of the word in brackets, for the given portion of a letter : 'Thank you for ______ (consider) my application. I look forward to working in your organization.'
questions.solution: considering

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Identify the error and supply the correction : Ninety-seven percent of the Earth's water is salty ocean water and another two percent is trapping in the Earth's ice caps and glaciers.
questions.solution: Error: trapping. Correction: trapped ("is trapped" — passive voice).

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Yukti and Sanjay had a conversation about going to a restaurant. Report Yukti's question : "Does this restaurant serve good South Indian food ?"
questions.solution: Yukti asked Sanjay whether/if that restaurant served good South Indian food.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Amit : Are you sure you can manage to go to the railway station on your own ?
Ananya : Oh yes! I have already booked a cab.
Amit asked Ananya ______ to go to the railway station on her own. Ananya replied in the affirmative and said that she had already booked a cab.
options: if she is sure she can manage
if she was sure she could manage
if she was sure to managing
questions.solution: In reported speech the tense moves back: 'are' becomes 'was' and 'can' becomes 'could'.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence from a book about 'Birds' : Each year, thousands of birds ______ southwards to avoid the harsh winter, embarking on an incredible journey that spans thousands of miles.
questions.solution: Birds 'migrate' (move seasonally). 'Immigrate' and 'emigrate' are used for people moving to or from a country to live.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Identify and correct the error in the line from an agency's advertisement : Tell us much about your project and we'll select suitable candidates for you to hire.
questions.solution: Error: much. Correction: more.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction : Obesity in teenage children is a major concern between parents today.
questions.solution: 'Between' is used for two; for many parents use 'among'.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Complete the narrative : Yesterday, Tanu walked to the park and ______ a breezy evening.
questions.solution: The sentence is in the simple past ('walked'), so 'enjoyed'.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Report the dialogue : Bhawna : I finished the project yesterday. Sohail : That's great ! Are you going to present it tomorrow ?
Bhawna told Sohail that ______. Sohail responded that it was great and asked if she were going to present it the next day.
questions.solution: she had finished the project the previous day / the day before.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Complete the notice : We are pleased to announce that our Annual Sports Day ______ on 30th April, 2025 at the school playground from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
questions.solution: The event is in the future, so the future passive 'will be held'.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Complete the slogan on "Save Earth" : Let's join hands, cultivate conservation, and ______ a greener tomorrow for generations to come.
questions.solution: It matches 'join' and 'cultivate' after 'Let's', so the base form 'ensure'.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Identify the error and supply the correction for the note in an air purifier's instruction manual : The plug should fit upto the outlet. If it doesn't fit, do not force it in.
questions.solution: Error: upto. Correction: into.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: You are Soumya Hansal / Sumit Hansal living at F-32, Shanti Nagar, Vayugarh. Seeing the inadequate healthcare infrastructure in your town, write a letter to the MLA of your area, in about 120 words, suggesting the need for improving existing healthcare facilities and creating more "Wellness Centres" including a specialized hospital for children and women.
questions.solution: Format (1 mark): sender's address, date, receiver (The MLA, Vayugarh), subject (Need for better healthcare facilities and Wellness Centres), salutation, complimentary close, name. Content (2 marks): the poor state of local healthcare (overcrowded government hospital, too few doctors and beds, long distances to travel, lack of equipment); the need to upgrade existing facilities; setting up Wellness Centres in each sector for preventive care and check-ups; a specialised hospital for women and children with maternity and paediatric care; a request for early action. Organisation and accuracy (2 marks): clear paragraphs, formal tone, correct grammar and spelling.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: You are Risha Khan / Zuhaan Khan, the sports captain of Highrise Public School, New Line, Rai Nagar. You believe that games and sports are an integral part of a student's life. Write a letter to the editor of a national daily, in about 120 words, sharing your views on the importance of physical education and suggesting the need to establish a dedicated sports university, so that students can pursue and focus on their favourite sport.
questions.solution: Format (1 mark): sender's address, date, The Editor, name of the newspaper, subject (Need for a dedicated sports university), salutation, close, name and designation. Content (2 marks): physical education builds fitness, discipline, teamwork and mental health; students are pushed towards academics only; talented young athletes lack proper coaching and facilities; a sports university would offer degrees, expert coaching, sports science and scholarships, letting students build careers in sport and bring laurels to the country; an appeal to the authorities. Organisation and accuracy (2 marks): clear paragraphs, formal tone, correct language.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
In the past few years, the teaching-learning process has gone beyond the four walls of the classroom. A chart compares E-learning and Classroom learning :
• E-learning: accessible anytime, anywhere; at your own pace; no travel costs, saves time.
• Classroom learning: same place, same time; caters to the needs of the class; transportation cost and time consuming.
Write an analytical paragraph in about 120 words, assessing the benefits and drawbacks of both, by selecting features that support your analysis.
questions.solution: Introduction (1 mark): learning has moved beyond the classroom; the chart compares two modes. Analysis (2 marks): e-learning is flexible, available anytime and anywhere and lets students learn at their own pace, saving travel time and cost; but it needs devices and internet and offers less personal interaction. Classroom learning happens at a fixed place and time and teaches at the pace of the whole class, with direct interaction with teachers and peers, but involves travel time and cost. Conclusion (1 mark): a blend of both may suit learners best. Accuracy (1 mark): correct, cohesive language within about 120 words.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Read the given details of a computer :
• electronic device that can store and process information
• makes life easy and simple
• physical description – monitor, keyboard, CPU and mouse
• computer technology used in all fields – education, medicine, commerce, entertainment
Analyse the details and write an analytical paragraph in about 120 words about the description and role of computers in today's world.
questions.solution: Introduction (1 mark): a computer is an electronic device that stores and processes information. Description and analysis (2 marks): its main parts are the monitor, keyboard, CPU and mouse; it makes life easier and simpler by doing complex tasks quickly; it is used in education (online classes, research), medicine (records, diagnosis), commerce (banking, online shopping) and entertainment (games, films, music). Conclusion (1 mark): computers have become indispensable, though they should be used wisely. Accuracy (1 mark): correct, cohesive language within about 120 words.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: A Letter to God
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions :
Not a leaf remained on the trees. The corn was totally destroyed. The flowers were gone from the plants. Lencho's soul was filled with sadness. When the storm had passed, he stood in the middle of the field and said to his sons, "A plague of locusts would have left more than this. The hail has left nothing. This year we will have no corn."
That night was a sorrowful one.
"All our work, for nothing."
"There's no one who can help us."
"We'll all go hungry this year."
(A Letter to God)
(i) Why were there no leaves left on the trees ? (A) The locusts ate them up. (B) An earthquake had occurred. (C) There was a hailstorm. (D) The animals grazed on them. (1)
(ii) Fill in the blank with the correct word : Lencho felt ______ (jubilant/devastated) when he saw his destroyed corn fields. (1)
(iii) When Lencho says, "All our work, for nothing," what does he refer to ? Explain in about 40 words. (2)
(iv) Why would Lencho have preferred a plague of locusts to a hailstorm ? (1)
questions.solution: (i) (C) There was a hailstorm. (ii) devastated. (iii) He means the whole year's hard work the family had put into growing the corn: ploughing, sowing and tending the field. The hailstorm destroyed the crop completely, so all that labour was wasted and they would have no harvest. (iv) Because locusts would have left at least some of the crop, while the hail left nothing at all.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: Footprints without Feet: The Thief's Story
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions :
Later, he patted me on the head and said never mind, he'd teach me to cook. He also taught me to write my name and said he would soon teach me to write whole sentences and to add numbers. I was grateful. I knew that once I could write like an educated man there would be no limit to what I could achieve.
It was quite pleasant working for Anil. I made the tea in the morning and then would take my time buying the day's supplies, usually making a profit of about a rupee a day. I think he knew I made a little money this way but he did not seem to mind.
(The Thief's Story)
(i) What does this line tell us about the character of Anil ? "I think he knew I made a little money this way but he did not seem to mind." (1)
(ii) Which best describes the realization Hari Singh had while working for Anil ? (A) that he would become a rich person one day (B) that Anil was a very intelligent master but a miser (C) that he would be able to accomplish a lot if he gets educated (D) that Anil made a lot of money from his job (1)
(iii) What did Anil promise to teach Hari Singh, and how did Hari Singh feel about the opportunity to learn ? Answer in about 40 words. (2)
(iv) Fill in the blank : The narrator earned extra money by making a/an ______ (profit/investment) of about a rupee a day. (1)
questions.solution: (i) Anil was kind, generous and trusting (tolerant of small faults). (ii) (C). (iii) Anil promised to teach him to cook, to write whole sentences and to add numbers, and taught him to write his name. Hari Singh was grateful and excited, believing that once he could write like an educated man there would be no limit to what he could achieve. (iv) profit.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: A Tiger in the Zoo
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions :
He stalks in his vivid stripes
The few steps of his cage,
On pads of velvet quiet,
In his quiet rage.
He should be lurking in shadow,
Sliding through long grass
(A Tiger in the Zoo)
(i) Identify and name any one figure of speech in the above extract. (2)
(ii) Fill in the blank with one word : The tiger's stalking on 'pads of velvet' suggests a movement that is ______. (1)
(iii) Which words would best describe the feelings of the tiger ? (A) Calm and content (B) Both subdued and angry (C) Both frustrated and happy (D) Both angry and famished (1)
(iv) Select the option that has the same rhyme scheme as the first four lines of the extract (stripes / cage / quiet / rage) :
(A) The people along the sand / All turn and look one way / They turn their back on the land / They look at the sea all day
(B) Along the sand, the people / All turn and look one way / They turn back on the sand / They look at the sea all day
(C) The people along the sand / Look one way and all turn / Their backs on the land / They look at the sea all day
(D) The people along the sand / They turn their back on the land / They look one way / At the sea all day (1)
questions.solution: (i) Any one: alliteration ('stalks in his vivid stripes'; 'should be lurking'; 'sliding'); metaphor ('pads of velvet'); oxymoron/transferred epithet ('quiet rage'). (ii) silent (soft). (iii) (B). (iv) (B): the extract rhymes abcb (only 'cage' and 'rage' rhyme), and so does option B (people / way / sand / day).

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: Nelson Mandela – Long Walk to Freedom
questions.text: Mandela in his speech says, "The policy of apartheid created a deep and lasting wound in my country and my people." Explain the significance of the word "wound" as used by Mandela. Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: A wound is a deep injury that hurts and takes long to heal. Apartheid caused long-lasting pain: racial discrimination, violence, loss of freedom and dignity, and broken families. Its damage to South African society and its people would take many years, perhaps generations, to heal.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: 'Dust of Snow', by Robert Frost is a poem about nature and simplicity. Elaborate. Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: The poem describes a simple moment: a crow shakes snow dust from a hemlock tree onto the poet. This small natural act changes his gloomy mood and saves part of a day he had regretted. Frost shows that nature, even through ordinary things like a crow and a hemlock, can heal and uplift us.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: Glimpses of India – Tea from Assam
questions.text: Explain the reasons for Rajvir's excitement on seeing the plantation and Pranjol's lack of enthusiasm. (Glimpses of India – Tea from Assam) Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: Rajvir was visiting a tea plantation for the first time; he had read a lot about tea and was amazed by the vast green sea of tea bushes and the pluckers at work. Pranjol had grown up on a tea estate in Assam, where his father was a manager, so the sight was ordinary for him.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: How to Tell Wild Animals
questions.text: Analyze how Wells employs humour, rhyme, and exaggerated traits to not only entertain, but also educate readers about various wild animals. (How to Tell Wild Animals) Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: Carolyn Wells uses a light, rhyming style and comic exaggeration: you know the lion when he roars at you, the bear when he hugs you, the hyena when it laughs as it eats you. The humour entertains, while each joke points to a real trait of the animal (the Asian lion's tawny colour, the tiger's stripes, the crocodile's tears, the chameleon's lack of colour), so readers learn while laughing.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Mijbil's transportation to England was no less than a nightmare for the author. Justify the statement using incidents from the lesson. (Mijbil the Otter) Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: Animals were not allowed on the airline, so Maxwell had to pack Mijbil in a box. Mijbil tore the box lining and bled, and on the plane he escaped and ran around the cabin, causing chaos: a woman screamed and passengers stood on seats. Maxwell crawled after him and finally caught him with the air hostess's help.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: Footprints without Feet: A Triumph of Surgery
questions.text: Analyze how Herriot uses Tricki and Mrs. Pumphrey's relationship to comment on societal attitudes towards pets and the responsibilities associated with their care. (A Triumph of Surgery) Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: Mrs Pumphrey loved Tricki but overfed and spoiled him with cream cakes, chocolates and malt, so he became fat and ill. Herriot shows that loving a pet is not the same as caring for it properly; a responsible owner gives a balanced diet and exercise. The 'surgery' was only a change of routine at his clinic.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: Footprints without Feet: The Book That Saved the Earth
questions.text: Today reading books is on the decline because of the prevalence of electronic media. Contrarily, earth is saved by a 'Book' in the chapter "The Book That Saved the Earth". Elaborate. Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: In the play, Martians planning to invade Earth find a book of Mother Goose nursery rhymes. Misreading rhymes like 'Humpty Dumpty' and 'Hey Diddle Diddle' as coded threats, they panic and abandon the invasion. So a simple book, read and misunderstood, saved the Earth, a humorous reminder of the power of books.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: Footprints without Feet: Footprints without Feet
questions.text: Discuss the character development of Griffin, as he grapples with the repercussions of his actions and attempts to navigate a world, where his once extraordinary abilities have become a burden. (Footprints without Feet) Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: Griffin, a brilliant scientist, made himself invisible but found it a burden: he was cold, homeless and hungry. Instead of using his gift well, he turned lawless, setting fire to his landlord's house, robbing a shop and Mr Hall's inn, and attacking people. His isolation made him more desperate and violent, until he had to flee.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: Amanda! / Madam Rides the Bus
questions.text: Amanda and Valli both represent a longing for freedom. Examine the above observation with reference to the two texts. (Amanda and Madam Rides the Bus) Answer in 100–120 words.
questions.solution: Amanda, constantly nagged by her mother about posture, chores and manners, escapes into daydreams of being a mermaid on a green sea, an orphan roaming free, or Rapunzel in a tower, all images of freedom from control. Valli, an eight-year-old village girl, longs to ride the bus to town; she secretly saves money, plans the trip and goes alone, showing independence and courage. Both girls want to make their own choices. Amanda's freedom is imagined, a reaction to restriction, while Valli acts on her wish and experiences the world, also learning about death and life on the way. Both texts show that children need space and freedom to grow.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: The Ball Poem / Nelson Mandela
questions.text: In 'The Ball Poem', Berryman explores the themes of loss, growing up, and transformation. Mandela also experienced loss of freedom and suffering along with his countrymen during his growing years on the basis of his race and colour. Compare and contrast the commonality of themes in both the texts. (The Ball Poem and Nelson Mandela – Long Walk to Freedom) Answer in 100–120 words.
questions.solution: Both texts deal with loss and the growth that comes from it. The boy in The Ball Poem loses his ball and learns, for the first time, that loss is part of life and that some things cannot be bought back; he grows up by learning to bear it. Mandela lost his freedom as a youth when he realised that, as a black man, his freedoms were an illusion under apartheid; he and his people suffered for years. The boy's loss is small and personal, while Mandela's is political and shared by a whole nation. Yet both turn loss into understanding: the boy matures, and Mandela becomes a fighter for everyone's freedom.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: Footprints without Feet: A Question of Trust
questions.text: Horace ends up in prison only to regret that a man should not trust anyone blindly without finding out the truth. Do you think his own foolishness was responsible for his arrest ? Give a reasoned answer. (A Question of Trust) Answer in 100–120 words.
questions.solution: Yes. Horace Danby, a clever safe-breaker, was careful in his planning but was fooled by a young woman who pretended to be the lady of the house. Charmed by her calm manner and her story of forgetting the combination, he trusted her without question, opened the safe without gloves and left his fingerprints everywhere. She took the jewels and he was arrested for a theft he did not complete. His pride, his weakness for flattery and his failure to check who she was made him a victim. Ironically, a thief who expected others to trust him failed to be suspicious himself, so his own foolishness led to his arrest.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Matilda's character embodies the journey of change or progression throughout the story, encapsulating the transformations she endured as a consequence of her experiences, trials, and engagements with other characters. In the light of the above information, trace the transformation seen in Matilda's character in the story. (The Necklace) Answer in 100–120 words.
questions.solution: At first Matilda Loisel is a pretty, discontented woman who dreams of luxury and feels her modest life is beneath her. At the ball, in a borrowed diamond necklace, she enjoys a moment of glory, but losing the necklace changes her life. To replace it, she and her husband borrow heavily and spend ten years in poverty: she dismisses the servant, does hard housework, bargains in shops and grows old and rough. Through this she becomes hardworking, responsible and strong. When she learns the necklace was fake, the irony shows how her vanity and pride cost her years of her life, and how hardship transformed her.
